JPM.rationale: JPM's fundamental health and trajectory are unambiguously strong: Q1 2026 delivered record revenue ($49.84B, +10% YoY) and EPS ($5.94, +17.2% YoY), Q2 2026 was even stronger with record net income of $21.2B ($7.70/share, +47% YoY) and revenue of $57.3B across every segment, ROE improved from 15.5% to 16.2%, and net margins are stable at 31.5%. The franchise is best-in-class with top market share across IB fees, trading, deposits, payments, and card issuance, and AUM crossed $5T. Consensus EPS estimates have been revised up 7.38% in the past 30 days with zero negative revisions. However, Pillar 2 (valuation) tempers the score significantly: P/B at 2.62x is near the top of its 2.2x-2.8x range after a 14% two-month re-rating, PE at 16.2x is mid-range but the stock is at the 96th percentile of its 52-week range ($350.85 vs $359.30 high), and the market has already priced much of the earnings improvement. Balance sheet leverage has increased (12.4x to 13.5x) with equity-to-assets declining from 8.1% to 7.4%. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst) is mixed: the Q2 earnings beat is already reported and priced, but upward estimate revisions and the $50B buyback authorization provide ongoing support. The Epstein-related allegations introduce unquantified tail risk around leadership. Dimon's own warnings about peak conditions and one-time events (SpaceX IPO) caution against extrapolating Q2's extraordinary results. Net: excellent franchise with strong trajectory, but valuation has already re-rated substantially, leaving a balanced rather than compelling risk-reward at current levels.
